author: Justin Couch
modifications: Consolidated independent suspension, wheel and drivetrain stepping behind IVehicleDynamics; no upstream scene globals or VehicleParent dependency.
Converted suspension spring/damping and propulsion/braking to SI forces and torque; finite body mass participates in all responses.

Finite-radius spherecast tire contact and tire forces use the owning PhysicsScene; equal and opposite forces on movable supporting bodies. The footprint is a simulation approximation for curb/driveway transitions.
Combined load-bounded tire forces replace acceleration-based slip defaults; ABS and traction limits based on contact load.
Automatic six-speed road-car gearbox with throttle-dependent downshift and finite shift interruption.
Added explicit Ackermann steering and anti-roll forces; no boost, burnout, stunt, air steering or rollover assist.
Simulation calibration only; no claim of measured Honda tire or suspension data.

Suspension damping uses contact-plane-relative travel speed divided by the suspension-axis projection. Corrected bridge grade response; verified both directions at 8 and 26.82 m/s with no chassis contacts.

Rolling resistance acts on residual longitudinal stopping demand after brake force, avoiding duplicate low-speed velocity cancellation. A configurable 40 ms low-speed tire response accounts for coupled body rotation instead of cancelling each wheel-point velocity in one explicit step. Anti-roll transfers normal load before tire grip and gravity compensation are calculated. Normal and tangential road reactions share the same physical contact point. All forces remain load-limited; no body pose or velocity is overwritten. Long stationary-queue and finite-impact regression fixtures cover this adaptation.
integration: Adapted/reimplemented core dynamics calculations, not the unmodified upstream component package.
